items.body: Long Story Short Dosed up on pretty high levels of reverb, Long Story Short is glistening, translucent music. Rain lightly falls as the bass note of an electric guitar sets the first stone in place. After that, soft sprinklings of notes are swept away on the perfumed, lilting air of major seventh chords. Appropriately titled ‘Lazing’, the music drifts by, seamlessly adding a little at a time. Like a cloud in the sky, it takes its time to fully form. Released on Too Many Fireworks, the ambient guitar music of Mateusz Franczak is sweet and soothing, at times lively and slightly frantic (which is unusual for the style of ambient guitar) without ever sounding cluttered, and at other times radiating a depthless serenity that ripples along with the reverb. The Polish experimental musician layers his ambient music with kindness, but there’s also a distorted, uneasy and thoroughly grey undercurrent in the depths of the ambient sound. That’s a mean feat in itself, because ambient music so often relies on its sparse vacuums that occupy the no-man’s-land between space and silence. The distorted intruder doesn’t dampen the slow, slightly melancholic feel, either. The notes ring and bleed together; the double stops clang with a muted tone that drags everything into a murky field of vision. A calming, casual tone captains the largely sedate music, its notes dimmed like the fine evening light of late spring. The shadows lurk just around the corner and are a couple of hours away from arriving, but as long as the music’s playing they never dare to creep out of their dark shells. A grittier sound sticks tightly to ‘Moving’. The prickly distortion is there, but it’s not strong enough to dampen the sound as a whole. The faces in the crowd appear to be crisper and sharper. Long Story Short takes a stride towards ambient song, too, the vocals gliding into a mini chorus that glows with the fiery heat of napalm. It gets its energy from both the soaring vocal and the spikier tone. Long Story Short lingers between structured song and improvised, sustaining soundscape, blearily straddling the ethereal and the everyday. Emerging out of this is a voice dripping with reverb, recalling the late Spacemen 3 and early Spritualized sound by way of a muddied, soulful drawl. The softer pools of a glorious, romanticized reverb evaporate in the light of a distorted tone that waddles out of the music’s swampy waters like a primeval crocodile. Paradise slips away and is replaced by the heady turbulence of uncertainty and doubt. The faith isn’t as strong as it was; the music’s glow is waning and swaying. Long Story Short is easily digestible, its colourful music as lulling as it is pressing. To a degree, Franczak’s history (he played in a number of rock and punk bands at an earlier age) influences the music’s lifeline, especially when it comes to the use of overdrive. It was, perhaps, inevitable, but it puts a different spin on the music. You get the feeling that Franczak really enjoyed the process. Long Story Short’s largely improvised, intoxicated melodies form a pleasant hybrid, where abrasive textures and passionate vocals blend in with ambient’s gentle curves. www.mateuszfranczak.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 波兰实验音乐人Mateusz Franczak的专辑《Long Story Short》以高浓度混响构建出晶莹剔透的氛围吉他音景。作品在氛围音乐的稀疏真空中融入失真与暗流，使表面甜美宁静的吉他音符下方始终涌动着一层灰暗、不安的底色。专辑在结构化歌曲与即兴声景之间游走，模糊了空灵与日常的边界，慵懒的低吟人声让人联想到Spacemen 3与早期Spiritualized。失真音色如史前鳄鱼般从沼泽般的混响中浮现，为浪漫化的音色增添粗粝质感。整体音乐如晚春暮光般柔和，同时又带着一丝摇摆的不确定与忧郁，在安抚与压迫之间维持张力。Franczak早年的摇滚与朋克经历为其氛围创作注入了过载音色，使这张专辑呈现出不同于常规氛围吉他作品的质地。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Adios K
items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

Weird and wonderful, it sounds
items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的数字EP，包含五首曲目，以传统音乐为根基，融入每位乐手的个人视角。主唱Mia Guldhammer是北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手，其说服力十足的声线成为专辑的核心。开篇曲以粗粝的奔跑节奏展示人声，簧口琴与风笛为唯一原创曲目提供推进力。扬琴为传统曲目营造细腻的织底，簧口琴与长笛、弦乐交织的终曲在器乐曲中呈现出令人不安的偏移感。整体笼罩着古老而粗粝的氛围，虽是首张作品却展现出超越新人阶段的成熟度。作为世界音乐领域的探索，它借助传统北欧器乐与民谣素材，但在实验性方面较为克制，融合手法偏保守，未深入触及前卫或即兴领域。

A body of water of a certain depth, not to be exceeded? The knowledge of our inner selves (or that of others), beyond which it may be dangerous to venture? The need to push past our own limits in order to grow? Or simply the name of a red wine from Abru
items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — *Limite Acque Sicure* by *Limite Acque Sicure*?a surprising title and surname, a sort of metaphor with multiple possible levels of meaning: the cartographic contours of the Mediterranean Sea in the Middle Ages? A body of water of a certain depth, not to be exceeded? The knowledge of our inner selves (or that of others), beyond which it may be dangerous to venture? The need to push past our own limits in order to grow? Or simply the name of a red wine from Abruzzo? Please refer to the very interesting lyrics on this album for a hint of an answer (be sure to have an Italian translation tool on hand if you don't speak the language). Musically speaking, you don't need to be an expert on Banco's music to understand that *Limite Acque Sicure*, hailing from Ferrara and formed in 2005 by singer Andrea Chendi and keyboardist Antonello Giovannelli as just one of many tribute bands, is a true devotee of the golden age of the Nocenzi brothers' band?a fact confirmed by the inclusion on this self-titled album of the iconic "Il Giardino Del Mago" (Banco 1972), in a dazzling live version.Between the introductory "Sogno D'Oriente" (12:48)?with its oriental sounds, as its name suggests, reminiscent of the famous "Kashmir"?and the short "Ti Salver� " (2:11)?placed at the other end, in the style and spirit of Banco's "Traccia II" (that album again) Certain tracks on *Limite Acque Sicure* stand out more. These are the ones where the band most clearly demonstrates that it has something personal to convey to us. "Terra Straniera" (7:53), with its majestic, enthusiastic, and determined finale, is closer in style to *Prowlers* than to *Banco*; "Il Respiro Dell'Anima" (8:25), with its more lively rhythm, ambitious structure, and shimmering arrangements that leave plenty of room for highly effective guitar and Moog solos. And above all, the epic "Fiamme Intorno " (10:48), with a darker main theme (though carried by a deceptively light rhythm), as if weighed down by a relentless exploration of humanity's spiritual wanderings, then giving way to a second, more open and luminous section, full of hope, whose coda?and this is quite unexpected?features a few drum beats dedicated to? Neil Peart. On a more contemporary note, the music of Limite Acque Sicure evokes memories of Museo Rosenbach, Campo Di Marte, Il Rovescio Della Medaglia, Alphataurus, and Apoteosi, all those meteor-like bands that shone for the duration of a single album (often released in 1973) before disappearing for a long time?or forever. "Limite Acque Sicure" seems to be a tribute to the RPI of the past, yet one that looks toward the future. In other words, it is less a relic of a glorious past than a promise of what the RPI may have in store.

items.body: Review by DimitrisTheHead — There is something about those late '60s/early '70s English albums, in contrast to the American ones, that make them sound epic. Is it the atmosphere? Is it the lyrics? Is it the keys? Is it something else? Maybe it is all these things combined. Now this record, has all that trademark elements of that era, it's bluesy, it's heavy, it's dark in some moments and happy on other moments, it's progy. "Repent Walpurgis" is an amazing instrumental and one of my favorites from that era. Matthew Fisher on the hammond, give me that same feeling, Jon Lord (Deep Purple) or Ken Hensley (Uriah Heep) give me when I'm listening to their records. Yes lads, it is that good.Procol Harum, as a typical British band, decided to leave "A whiter shade of pale" off of the UK vinyl release and put it just on the North America release, plus they left some amazing songs as bonus tracks. (Just listen "Homburg"!!!)A must listen for the fans of that era.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / progressive rock / crossover prog
items._cn_summary: 这张1967年的英国专辑融合了布鲁斯、重型摇滚与早期前卫元素，编曲中大量运用Hammond风琴营造出史诗般的氛围，曲目在黑暗与明亮之间交替切换。器乐作品尤其突出，Hammond的演奏具有浓郁的年代感与重量感，与同时代Deep Purple的Jon Lord、Uriah Heep的Ken Hensley风格相近。值得一提的是，乐队在不同地区发行版本上曲目安排有所差异，北美版收录了传唱度极高的单曲，而英国版则将更多作品作为附赠曲目发行。整体而言，这张唱片保留了六十年代末英国乐队特有的气质，器乐编排扎实，氛围营造到位，但并未突破传统摇滚的框架，属于早期前卫摇滚的典型代表作品。

An album unexpectedly devoid of Mikael �kerfeldt's guttural vocals, the brutal riffs and abrasive textures that had defined the Swedish band, and their us
items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Recorded simultaneously with its hostile and murky counterpart, "Deliverance", during the summer of 2002, the gentler and more melancholic "Damnation" - Opeth's seventh album - didn't see the light of day until April 2003, due to their record label's decision to separate the two releases for commercial reasons. An album unexpectedly devoid of Mikael �kerfeldt's guttural vocals, the brutal riffs and abrasive textures that had defined the Swedish band, and their usual monolithic instrumental displays, the result of �kerfeldt's deliberate intention to immerse himself in the smoother, more experimental side of 1970s progressive rock, accompanied for this purpose by the fantastic Steven Wilson, whose decisive work as co-producer and musician brings a sensibility and sonic aesthetic that resonate with those of his band, Porcupine Tree.While it's true that in their earlier work Opeth included acoustic and refreshing sections amid their stormy arrangements, on "Damnation" they take it a step further by devoting its just over forty-three minutes to dreamy melodies set in an introspective and tense atmosphere that flows unhurriedly over the misty, ethereal soundscapes woven by Wilson's Mellotrons and Peter Lindgren's clean, serene guitars. Tracks like the hypnotic "Windowpane," with its magnificent jazz-inspired solo, or the psychedelic "In My Time of Need," "Death Whispered a Lullaby," and "Closure" evoke the most dreamlike and hazy side of genre icons such as King Crimson, the pre-"The Dark Side of the Moon" Pink Floyd, and the Gabriel-era Genesis.And staying true to that evocative, immersive vibe, the instrumental "Ending Credits," with its long guitar bends reminiscent of Camel's Andy Latimer, and the impeccable backing -as throughout the album- from the standout Mart�n M�ndez on bass and Martin Lopez on percussion, along with the trance-like and unchanging "Weakness," featuring a whispering, spectral �kerfeldt, ultimately round out "Damnation": the beginning of Opeth's stylistic transition and one of the most controversial phases of their career.3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive rock / experimental / acoustic / 70s prog influenced
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Opeth与同时期录制的《Deliverance》形成鲜明对比的作品，刻意剥离了死亡咆哮唱腔与极端金属编制，转向七十年代前卫摇滚的柔和实验面。Steven Wilson担任联合制作人并贡献Mellotron音色，与乐队共同营造出朦胧、梦幻的声景氛围。专辑以原声吉他与爵士化独奏为主轴，曲目如《Windowpane》《In My Time of Need》透露出King Crimson、前Pink Floyd与Gabriel时期Genesis的影响。器乐曲目《Ending Credits》以悠长吉他滑音呼应Camel的Andy Latimer，整体氛围内省缓慢。然而，尽管带有实验色彩，这仍是根植于传统前卫摇滚范畴内的作品，与用户偏好的自由即兴、电子实验或暗潮工业等方向距离较远。评论本身信息充分，引用了多位乐手贡献并分析了音乐结构。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — After a long-term hiatus (last good album released in 1981), Collegium Musicum returned at least to the stage in 1997 with the original members of which Freso remained in a particular good shape. The choice of tracks performed was good as it didn't only feature the first two albums but reached later into their career. I am personally a bigger fan of their 1971-1975 period rather than their first eponymous album.The guest Andrej Seban provides elastic guitar while Hajek hasn't lost his edge on the drums.I'm not very content with Varga though because I find his playing somehow sloppy - as if he couldn't hit all the right keys, or not always on time. This suspicion raised with me in the beginning of the first track but hasn't evaporated later. Or is it just the not keyboard sound which does not allow for careful key distinction?In any case, this was the first official live album with their classic songs, however the double live album from 2010 could be more appealing.
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / live album
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是斯洛伐克前卫摇滚乐队Collegium Musicum在1997年重组后的现场录音，标志乐队在长期沉寂后的回归演出。曲目选择跨越了乐队多个时期的代表作，覆盖范围较为广泛。评论者认为鼓手Hajek依旧保持了锋利的节奏感，客座吉他手Andrej Seban的弹性演奏也为现场增色不少。然而，键盘手Varga的演奏被指出存在明显瑕疵——音准不够精准，时机把控偶有失误，评论者推测这或许与现场键盘音色本身的清晰度不足有关。作为乐队首张官方现场专辑，它记录了乐队经典作品的现场演绎版本，但评论者暗示2010年的双张现场专辑在现场表现和制作质量上更具吸引力。整体而言，这是一次具有历史意义的回归演出，但在演奏精度上未能达到评论者的期望。

items.body: Dark synthwave producer Das Mörtal releases the two-track single “DRAIN ME” on Lisbon Lux Records on 30 September 2026. The single pairs the original version with a remix by synthwave producer Dan Terminus, and precedes Das Mörtal’s mini-album “DECVY I,” out 29 October 2026. Das Mörtal, the project of Montreal-based producer Cristóbal Cortes, describes “DRAIN ME” as “a track about the feeling of running in circles in the health care system while being drained from the multiple tests one person might go through.” The track opens with a cinematic, sweeping tone before shifting into a fast-paced, techno-driven rhythm section with an arpeggiated synth pluck, washed-out vocals and a half-time breakdown before its final chorus. Dan Terminus, grouped alongside Perturbator, Carpenter Brut and GosT as one of what press materials call the “Four Horsemen of Synthwave,” reworks “DRAIN ME” with chopped and manipulated vocals, punchy percussion and an occasional violin line over booming basslines that combine acoustic and synthesised elements. “DRAIN ME” follows the double single “Parasite & Ghost,” which Das Mörtal released on Lisbon Lux Records on 4 June 2026, also ahead of “DECVY I.” An official teaser for “DRAIN ME” is available on YouTube, and the single is available to pre-save via ffm.to/drainmee. About Das Mörtal Das Mörtal is the project of Cristóbal Cortes, an electronic music producer and DJ based in Montreal whose work began in Berlin, drawing on artists including Steve Moore and Aphex Twin. Das Mörtal’s sound blends techno, occult electro and Italo disco into a dark, nostalgic style informed by German techno as well as horror and science-fiction soundtracks. Das Mörtal has released material including the double single “Parasite & Ghost” (2026), the “Bury the Sorrow” and “Hotline Miami II” EPs, and the “Miami Beach Witches” album, among other releases on Bandcamp. The project has performed close to 100 shows since 2015, including more than 70 dates across the United States and Europe, at festivals such as Osheaga, Transmusicales de Rennes, FME and MEG Festival, and on tour with Vitalic, Perturbator and Carpenter Brut. “DRAIN ME” is Das Mörtal’s second single of 2026 on Lisbon Lux Records, after “Parasite & Ghost” in June.
items._cn_summary: Das Mörtal 是一支来自蒙特利尔的暗潮合成器项目，主脑 Cristóbal Cortes。2026年9月发行的双曲单曲收录原创版与 Dan Terminus 的混音版，后者的版本以切碎的人声、强劲打击乐与小提琴线条相结合，在合成器低音与原声元素之间游走。原创版从电影化的铺陈进入techno驱动的节奏段落，加入琶音合成器音色与半拍breakdown。作品主题围绕在医疗系统中反复奔走、身心被消耗的感受展开，延续项目一贯的暗黑怀旧风格，融合techno、occultech electro与Italo disco等元素。Lisbon Lux Records为独立小厂牌。该文偏向新闻通稿性质，缺乏深度评论与艺术分析。

items.body: West Palm Beach dance-punk trio Violet Silhouette released the single “This Is Something” on 25 September 2026, with a video directed by Roberto Badillo. The track pairs post-punk structures with dance rhythms, with reference points close to early Human League and LCD Soundsystem. Violet Silhouette is Dan, Zaii and Lily Vile (bass), formed in West Palm Beach, Florida in late 2019 and now based between South Florida and Austin, Texas. This Is Something by Violet Silhouette Violet Silhouette’s video for ‘This Is Something’ Roberto Badillo directed the video for “This Is Something,” which the band says draws on David Lynch’s 1997 film “Lost Highway.” Violet Silhouette described the concept: “Visually, we drew from David Lynch’s Lost Highway. Our friend Roberto Badillo took our vision and ran with it, the result is sleek and visceral, like a gloved hand dragging desire across the table.” About Violet Silhouette Violet Silhouette formed in West Palm Beach, Florida in late 2019. The band is Dan, Zaii and Lily Vile (bass), now split between South Florida and Austin, Texas. Prior releases include the single “Strange Wind” and “Hierda Demonica,” a track from a second EP, alongside the “Feverblue” release on the band’s Bandcamp page. Violet Silhouette has been producing a debut full-length, “VIVID(IS)DECAY,” entirely in-house since 2024. “This Is Something,” released 25 September 2026, is the band’s latest single. Its video, directed by Roberto Badillo, is the most recent visual release tied to the band’s upcoming album.
items._cn_summary: 西棕榈滩三人乐队 Violet Silhouette 发布单曲《This Is Something》，将后朋克的骨架与舞曲节奏相结合，参考坐标靠近早期 Human League 与 LCD Soundsystem。乐队成员 Dan、Zaii 与贝斯手 Lily Vile 于 2019 年底在佛罗里达组建，目前活动于南佛罗里达与德州奥斯汀之间，过去曾发表《Strange Wind》《Hierda Demonica》以及 Bandcamp 上的《Feverblue》。MV 由 Roberto Badillo 执导，视觉灵感取自大卫·林奇 1997 年电影《Lost Highway》，乐队形容其观感'如同一只戴着手套的手将欲望拖过桌面'，呈现冷峻而感官的质感。乐队自 2024 年起独立制作全长专辑《VIVID(IS)DECAY》，该单曲是这张即将发行的专辑中最新释出的视觉作品。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — The first APP album has captured hearts of many progressive and pop enthusiasts.It sounded contemporary, even futuristic (vocal vocoder) with the clean, imaginative production and the great concept selection with the another Al(l)an, Edgar Alan Poe.In comparison to the later albums, music is not that radio friendly yet and music keeps being ambitious and focused, where the duel among vocalists vs instrumentals are pretty levelled.The band shows knack for emotional ballads ("The Cask of Amontillado", "To one in paradise") which will be perfected on other albums. I have always liked the symbiose of emotional music, great studio talent (no surprise when speaking of Alan Parsons) and curious instrumentals. The flagship of all APP instrumentals is presented on the second side of the album "The fall of the house of Usher". It comprises 5 parts, all of them both progressive and symphonic without any playing excesses.No wonder this album belongs to the highest acclaimed APP albums and carved a unique blend of styles on the European music map.
items._genre: crossover prog / symphonic prog / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Alan Parsons Project首张专辑，以Edgar Allan Poe的文学作品为概念框架，将叙事性歌词与管弦乐化的摇滚编制结合。制作上强调干净的录音室工艺和声码器等当时具有未来感的声音处理。专辑分为两半：前半偏向带有情感旋律的人声曲目，后半以《The Fall of the House of Usher》为核心的多乐章器乐组曲最为突出，展现出交响化与渐进摇滚的融合手法。评论指出该作相较后期更显野心，人声与器乐的张力较为均衡，乐队的情绪化抒情传统在此初步成形。整体属于七十年代欧洲艺术摇滚脉络中的概念专辑制作，融合了文学性主题与精致的录音室美学。

items.body: Italian EBM and industrial duo Alien Vampires will release their 2010 album “Harshlizer” on vinyl for the first time on November 30, 2026, through Alfa Matrix. The LP is limited to 300 copies worldwide, priced at €18.99, with no repress planned. ‘Harshlizer’ vinyl: format and tracklist The vinyl edition carries new artwork designed specifically for the LP format and reproduces the original ten-track album across two sides: A-side: “No Way Back” “Evil Bloody Music” “She’s On Drugs (more than me)” “See You In Hell (feat. Suicide Commando)” “Harshlizer” B-side: “Lies” “Control The Universe” “Nothing To Lose” “Far Away” “Her Blood Into My Veins” “Harshlizer” marked the start of Alien Vampires’ relationship with Alfa Matrix when it was first released in 2010, and includes “See You In Hell,” the duo’s collaboration with Suicide Commando. A digital version of the album, expanded with the “Industrializer” bonus disc of additional tracks and remixes released in 2024, remains available on Bandcamp. Harshlizer + Industrializer (Bonus Version) by Alien Vampires Part of the Alfa Matrix Essentials vinyl series The “Harshlizer” LP is part of Alfa Matrix Essentials, a vinyl reissue series tied to the label’s 25th anniversary that brings catalogue albums to the format for the first time. Alien Vampires previously released the limited-edition LP “Kinky To Hell” on solid red vinyl through Alfa Matrix in 2022. About Alien Vampires Alien Vampires is an Italian industrial, EBM and dark electro duo formed in 2003 by Nysrok Infernalien, who handles guitars and keyboards, alongside Nightstalker on keyboards and drums. The project released its debut single, “I’m Dead Fuck You,” in 2004, followed by the album “Evil Generation” in 2005 through Kold Finger. After the 2007 EP “Nuns Are Pregnant” and the album “No One Here Gets Out Alive” through BLC Productions, Alien Vampires released “Fuck Off and Die!” in 2009. “Harshlizer” arrived in 2010 as the duo’s first release through Alfa Matrix, a relationship that has continued since. Alfa Matrix issued a deluxe two-CD version of “Harshlizer” paired with the bonus disc “Industrializer” in February 2024, gathering additional tracks and remixes from the same period as the original album. Alien Vampires continued with the EPs “Clubbers Die Younger” (2012), “Hard Drugs & BDSM” (2014), “World in Denial” and “Destrudo” (both 2020), and the albums “Drag You to Hell” (2015), “Evil Degeneration Offspring” (2017) and “Fuck The Revolution Bring On The Apocalypse” (2018). “Drag You to Hell” featured collaborations with members of Ministry, Mayhem and Psyclon Nine. The duo’s most recent album, “Return Me To Hell,” followed in 2023 with a cover of Skinny Puppy’s “Assimilate” featuring former Slipknot drummer Joey Jordison, in one of his final recordings before his death.
items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇关于意大利工业电子二人组Alien Vampires 2010年专辑《Harshlizer》首次发行黑胶的新闻资讯。文章介绍了限量300张、价格18.99欧元的黑胶版本发行细节，包含A面与B面的曲目列表，以及该专辑作为二人组与厂牌Alfa Matrix合作起点的历史背景。专辑收录了与Suicide Commando合作曲目《See You In Hell》。文章还追溯了乐队从2003年成立至今的发展脉络，列出了后续EP与专辑作品，并提及2024年发行的双CD豪华版加入了额外的混音曲目。作为一篇信息性较强的厂牌发行公告，文章缺乏对音乐本身的深入评论，未涉及声音设计、制作手法或艺术价值的具体分析，仅提供编年史式的资料整理，对读者了解音乐内容帮助有限。

items._cn_summary: 细野晴臣阔别七年的录音室专辑，以新冠疫情与人工智能冲击为背景，探讨孤独与混乱之后走向调和的主题。专辑以混入孩童声音的玩具电子乐开场，曲目涵盖翻唱经典并填入日语歌词的作品、温和摇曳的电声民谣，以及对李斯特乐章的哼唱改编。十分钟容量的十首短曲构成一段宁静而私密的时光，整体气质温柔内敛，既具个人化表达又试图触及普遍情感。作品偏向氛围化轻量制作，融合电子声学元素与民谣质感，在细野的创作谱系中延续了一贯的轻盈哲学，但实验性较为克制，更接近舒适聆听范畴。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于艺术家在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，以园中最古老的一棵棕榈树为起点，讲述其2021年被砍伐后发现的植物学真相——原来它并非百年来人们以为的百慕大棕榈，而是墨西哥棕榈。整张作品以人声和钢琴为核心，辅以轻柔的氛围音景设计，营造出亲密而庄重的氛围。评论者特别指出钢琴演奏者Dave Milligan的演绎富有共情力，而Polwart温暖且具有悲悯感的声线将自然、历史与个人记忆编织在一起。虽然表面上形式朴素、克制，但专辑在内容上具有史诗般的纵深，是为一棵老树谱写的安魂曲，也寄托了对未来的希望。整体偏向当代民谣与声音艺术的跨界创作。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 挪威二人组Sudan Dudan的第五张专辑《Mørke refrenger》以原声吉他为主轴，搭配小提琴、langeleik琴、里拉琴、口簧琴等北欧传统乐器，辅以人声和声。专辑标题意为"暗色副歌"，歌词涉及大地、星辰、失落与哀伤等主题，带有沉思气质。编曲上既有偏传统的挪威tralling人声吟唱，也有借用法国知名旋律加以变奏的轻盈段落，末曲罕见地加入电吉他，深沉twang音色令人联想到Duane Eddy或David Lynch配乐。整体制作精良，想象力丰富，是一张在传统民谣框架内进行有限探索的专辑。

items._cn_summary: 该专辑由诗人Anne Waldman与Thurston Moore、James Ilgenfritz及Anagram Ensemble合作，将切割诗作（cut-up poetry）与切割音乐（cut-up music）并置，呈现出文字与声响之间的非线性碰撞。Anne Waldman作为垮掉一代后裔的诗人，其朗诵本身即具有强烈的表演性与实验色彩；Thurston Moore的吉他与低音提琴/作曲家的乐器编制则提供即兴与自由演奏的底色。专辑需要完整聆听才能理解其结构逻辑与层次关系，乐评仅提供了极短的导语式描述，缺少对具体曲目、文本内容或音乐手法的深入分析。由于正文内容过短（不足200字符），且更像是一段转载摘要而非完整乐评，信息密度不足以支撑对该作品艺术水准与创新性的深入判断。整体来看，这是一张跨越诗歌与即兴音乐的跨界实验作品，但可用信息极为有限。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The use of synthesizers and the Mellotron, combined with an abrasive, dense hard rock sound, defined Black Bonzo's debut as progressive hard rock; vocalist Magnus Lindgren, with his very clean voice, and keyboardist Nicklas Ahlund, capable of playing everything from rock 'n' roll to classical organ passages, evoke the more daring side of Deep Purple, while on the title track, "Lady of the Light," they also create an almost cinematic, eerie atmosphere."Brave Young Soldier" also features psychedelia, rhythmic shifts, and dissonances that greatly enrich the track; once again, Magnus Lindgren demonstrates his own distinct personality and style, avoiding the path of other singers in the genre. Guitar and organ combine for a brilliant riff at the end, blending a medieval past with rock music evocative of spells and stone forests."Fantasy World" evoked a different atmosphere, reminiscent of Wishbone Ash; "Freedom," on the other hand, could easily have appeared on Queen's debut album. The melody ultimately took center stage, a gothic, operatic tune that kept evolving. While this didn't necessarily contribute to the album's cohesion, the diversity added emotional depth, featuring the Mellotron from "Sirens" and, above all, the drumming, which, combined with the acoustic guitar, recalled King Crimson's debut.On one hand, there is the clenched-teeth rock and tight sound of "Jailbait," and the dark, ominous lyricism of "Leave Your Burdens", complete with Black Sabbath-style riffs reminiscent of their bluesier moments, while the hypnotic conclusion of "Where the River Meets the Sea" serves as the perfect finale. It clearly defines an artistic vision that was at once velvet and steel, possessing scales and gills to dive through the ocean, yet also lungs to scream and fill with air in order to fly.
items._genre: progressive hard rock / heavy prog / psychedelic rock
items._cn_summary: 这张2004年的瑞典处女作将Mellotron与合成器嵌入厚重的硬摇滚骨架，主唱Magnus Lindgren以干净的声线游走于Deep Purple式的大胆与Queen式的旋律之间。键盘手Nicklas Ahlund横跨摇滚律动与古典管风琴段落，标题曲营造出近似配乐式的诡异氛围，而"Brave Young Soldier"则通过迷幻色彩、节奏突变与不协和音制造张力。"Fantasy World"让人联想到Wishbone Ash，"Freedom"则呈现哥特式歌剧旋律的演化轨迹。整体专辑在硬摇滚框架内进行风格拼贴，黑安息日式的蓝调riff与King Crimson首专的鼓击+原声吉他质感交替出现，但这种多样性也削弱了整体凝聚力。评论以文学化笔法描述乐队在金属器乐与旋律氛围之间的平衡，但对声音设计层面的深度分析较为有限。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Reale Accademia Di Musica is a italien band from Rome, best known among us for its self-titled debut album released in 1972, an Italian progressive rock sound similar to that of PFM from the same era, though lacking the Milanese band's charisma. The rest of their discography, led by composer Adriano Monteduro under the acronym RAM, is of much less interest to us? until their 2018 revival spearheaded by Pericle Sponzilli, the band's original guitarist, who enlisted the talents of virtuoso keyboardist Fabio Liberatori (a prolific composer of Italian film scores) and Erika Savastani, a young singer with a powerful voice, to release *Angeli Mutanti* that year?an interesting, if not essential, fusion of modern Italian pop and flamboyant, timeless Italian progressive rock.*Lame Di Luce* is in the same vein, while at times drawing closer to the Italian neo-prog of the '90s (Leviathan, Mad Crayon?) as on the magnificent "Ascesa al Fuji," one of those gems that seems to smile at us and make life so sweet as it comes alive with vibrant colors. Fifty years later, the pastoral feel of the debut album is very much present on "Onde di Sabbia," and a few other echoes of the RPI masters charm us effortlessly (Le Orme on "Due Pietre Preziose Birmane" or Banco on the jazzy "Si Parler�"). This band excels at writing melodies that are out of the ordinary while remaining accessible to a wide audience, as heard on the irresistible "Lame di Luce," which seems to be to Italian song what the Moody Blues' music was to English prog: sophisticated pop without being ostentatious, capable of sounding harmonious even to the most delicate angels in heaven. The final quarter-hour of *Lame di Luce* may seem a bit weaker. "Una Ferita da Disinfettare" is a well-crafted symphonic prog track, but it will primarily catch our attention for a brief, unexpected quote from the famous guitar solo in "Firth of Fifth." "Ore Lente" could pass for a simple, dynamic song with a catchy chorus, and "Incontri" for a nostalgic Pink Floyd-style ballad that's a bit too slow?were it not for the cinematic influence of Fabio Liberatori, which enriches the mood and atmosphere of both tracks.Ultimately, the best moments carry the album and overshadow the few, quite excusable weaknesses, ensuring that our favorable opinion remains. *Lame di Luce* is a pleasant surprise and deserves our full attention. All it needs are a few more instrumental developments to make it an excellent modern RPI album worthy of its illustrious predecessors, among whom *Reale Accademia Di Musica* was counted in the early '70s.
items._genre: Italian progressive rock / neo-prog / symphonic prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是意大利罗马乐队在沉寂五十年后的回归之作，延续了七十年代意大利前卫摇滚的传统风格。乐队由原始吉他手领军，邀来资深键盘手和年轻女歌手，将现代意大利流行与华丽古典的前卫摇滚相融合。部分曲目靠近九十年代意大利新前卫的路线，旋律出众却保持平易近人；另一些作品则回溯首张专辑的田园气质，并巧妙融入其他大师的影子。键盘手的电影配乐背景为慢板曲目增添了画面感与情绪厚度。然而，专辑末段约十五分钟的作品相对平淡，器乐展开也不够充分。作为一张延续前辈荣光的现代意大利前卫摇滚专辑，整体听感愉悦但在实验性和创新性上偏保守，与实验、前卫爵士、电子等偏好领域的交集有限。

items.body: Review by Warthur — Bakerloo's sole album reveals them as a truly diverse progressive group of the early prog era. They've clearly emerged from the same blues rock primordial soup formented by the Yardbirds and Bluesbreakers and Cream and which saw peers like Jetbro Tull and Black Sabbath emerge. Bakerloo actually shared a manager with Sabbath, but it's Tull who you'll be reminded of most - in particular, the sound of their earliest days, before Mick Abrahams left. There's no flute, but plenty of harmonica - and the power trip work in enough influences from jazz and classical music to suggest a group just as broad in influences as Tull, though perhaps with more influence from the calmer, more meditative side of psychedelia creeping in at points.It's no surprise that they fell by the wayside at the end - this was a crowded scene, after all, and it was all too easy for groups to get lost in the shuffle, and with Tull already evolving away from their early blues influences and Black Sabbath turning the blues into doom metal their peers were moving to distinguish themselves, so you can see why Bakerloo were in danger of being eclipsed. In retrospect, it's a gem of its particular scene - it's just that the scene in question was on the cusp of being overtaken by other strands of prog and blues-derived rock.
items._cn_summary: 这张1969年的专辑被视为早期前卫摇滚萌芽阶段的产物，乐评将其置于布鲁斯摇滚转向前卫摇滚的关键转型期。乐队从Yardbirds、Cream等布鲁斯摇滚土壤中生长出来，作品中融合了爵士与古典音乐的影响，同时带有迷幻摇滚冥想式的平静气质。口琴替代了长笛成为主要旋律乐器，呼应了Jethro Tull早期在Ian Anderson接手之前的声音特征。乐评指出乐队因同期Tull与Black Sabbath迅速确立各自风格而逐渐被历史边缘化，但这张专辑作为那个特定场景的结晶仍具有回顾价值。整体属于过渡时期作品，融合元素有限，未触及更深层的实验或前卫探索。

items.body: Review by alainPP — An evolving, melodic, synth-driven sound; the track evokes human degradation in the face of AI."Tears Of The Muse" kicks off as a dark, mid-tempo rock track featuring 80s-style keyboards?somewhere between rock, prog, and dark wave. A thunderous beat reminiscent of Genesis and Gabriel gives way to a sharp riff and vocals that trade lines with a vocoder. "EKO" features a hook redolent of Saga?think sugary new-millennium prog-metal with Martin stepping in for Damian. A dash of Arena, a touch of Lalu?it works perfectly for this groovy track with its driving bassline. "I Am The One" features piano accompanying Simon's metronomic drumming. It has a rich, proggy sound?like Toto?complemented by a heavy riff and a solo from Joop. There's a groovy, jazzy, Yes-style break leading into a warm choral finale. "Mayacama" is an instrumental that channels Toto and Saga?I can't help but hear the resemblance. A guitar groove underpins the melody, building into a progressive crescendo with the keyboards following suit. A piano break and a synth-led ballad section precede Joop showing off his dexterity. "Prince With The Swift Warning" features rolling pads and vocal harmonies that add complexity, navigating between rock, pop, and ballad styles. It includes a tense break with a sharp guitar solo, an infectious rhythm, and a second solo that is delicate, bluesy, and proggy."Learning To Fly" features airy vocals and echoes of Saga?or even Marillion. It's an accessible track that surprises with its evolution, while a dark organ keeps the listener on edge. The guitar solo is pure prog, leading into a riff where Martin shows off his impressive vocal range, backed by Simon. The finale soars as Joop and then Vivien drive the track to a spine-tingling climax. "A Drop Of Water" is an acoustic guitar interlude featuring a brilliant, ear-piercing arpeggio?a nod to Steve Howe of Yes. "Fhloston Paradise"?named after the station in *The Fifth Element*?blends hard-hitting rock and vocoder with the energetic, percussive groove characteristic of Joop, reminiscent of Iron Maiden. It features a Yes-style coda, confirming Vivien's admiration for the band. "Cordal Weaves" is a unique track with ethereal, searching notes and a stereo soundscape that creates a distinctly progressive atmosphere. It offers a funky, simmering moment: Martin rallies the energy, Joop lays into the rhythm, and Simon unleashes a barrage of drums. The finale features soaring vocals and a guitar full of melancholic longing. "Midnight Ink" serves as a piano-bar-style closer, driven by a poignant, whispered croon. Melancholic strings lend the track a solemn tone?the perfect way to wrap up the album.A melting pot of mainstream rock in the vein of Saga, Yes, and Toto, created above all for the sheer joy of it. It offers a softer take on prog metal and an intense jazz-prog vibe that feels like a journey in a time capsule.
items._genre: progressive metal / melodic rock / synth-driven prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以合成器驱动的旋律化前卫金属为核心，融合了八十年代暗潮键盘音色与经典前卫摇滚元素。从开篇的黑暗中速摇滚到加入人声编码器的电子化处理，再到钢琴伴奏的抒情段落与爵士化过渡，整体在Saga、Yes、Toto等老牌乐队的影子下构建了一种怀旧而包容的声音。器乐编排扎实，鼓击稳健，吉他独奏兼具布鲁斯味与技巧性，键盘主导的氛围营造贯穿始终。专辑后期出现原声吉他间奏与钢琴酒廊式收尾，显示出对曲式多样性的追求。然而，尽管乐评中提到了一些实验性编排如立体声空间处理和功能性突破段落，整张作品仍然建立在主流旋律摇滚框架之上，对前卫金属的探索偏保守，更偏向于旋律化、情感化的传统prog-metal表达，适合喜爱经典前卫摇滚的听众。

items.body: BY GLOWBALL Since launching in 2024, GLOWBALL FESTIVAL has placed electronic music at its core, combining music, visual art, performance, subculture, and international exchange. Over the past three years, GLOWBALL has evolved from a festival rooted in global dance music culture and interdisciplinary creation into a longer-term practice encompassing international curation, artist collaboration, and exchange between cultural scenes. By 2026, GLOWBALL’s activities had expanded beyond the annual festival itself. In May, the team and participating artists travelled to Lyon, France, to collaborate with and perform at Nuits sonores. In June, GLOWBALL returned to Taipei for its third edition, followed in August by participation in talks, exhibitions, and international industry exchange at TMEX. From Taiwan to Lyon and back to Taipei, this journey across several months gradually outlined GLOWBALL’s evolving role as a platform for electronic music culture. Rather than repeating the same festival format from year to year, GLOWBALL continuously reconsiders the relationships between electronic music and other creative disciplines, cultural communities, and international networks. Music remains both the central artistic medium and a means through which these connections can be formed. 2024: Building a Foundation for Cross-Disciplinary Encounters through Global Dance Music Culture The name GLOWBALL began as a play on the word “global,” combining the luminous imagery of “glow” with the multiple associations of “ball”—a dance, a sphere, and a gathering. From the outset, GLOWBALL was never confined to a particular genre of electronic music. Instead, it explored how artists and practices from different regions, cultural backgrounds, and creative disciplines could coexist within a shared festival environment. International and Taiwanese musicians, DJs, new media artists, dancers, and performers were brought together under the same event, allowing the festival to become a site where different cultural practices could intersect. From its first edition, Ballroom culture, Indigenous culture, new media art, A/V live performance, contemporary dance, and electronic music all formed part of GLOWBALL’s landscape. Rather than defining itself through a single musical genre, the festival developed a framework centered on electronic music while allowing different cultures and creative methodologies to exist side by side. 2025: From Coexistence to Collaboration—Developing Cross-Disciplinary Production Methods The second edition, based on the theme of “Ping Pong”, placed greater emphasis on collaboration and interaction. Rather than simply bringing diverse acts together under one lineup, GLOWBALL paired them up to create shared performances. Electronic music was combined with traditional instrumentation, dance, artificial intelligence, motion capture, A/V live performance, and other disciplines. Through the joint production of different sounds, cultures, and artistic practices, interdisciplinary collaboration became an important part of GLOWBALL’s approach. That year, the festival worked with collectives and communities representing different cities and subcultural scenes, including HE.SHE.THEY., Over My Body, TYO GQOM, and Formosa Sound System. This broadened GLOWBALL’s focus beyond individual performers to include their cultural scenes as part of the programme too. International electronic music and party communities met local Taiwanese networks around sound system culture, Ballroom, drag, and queer culture, creating opportunities for both coexistence and exchange within the festival. GLOWBALL thus began moving beyond conventional festival programming centered on booking individual artists, developing instead into a platform connecting different cultural scenes. 2026: Building Two-Way International Exchange and Long-Term Networks The third edition built upon the previous year’s collaborations with different scenes and collectives, while expanding these relationships into longer-term exchanges across cities and national borders. The collaboration with Lyon-based Nuits sonores began in May, when GLOWBALL travelled to Lyon to curate performances and exchange programmes. It continued in June, when Nuits sonores Artistic Director Pierre Zeimet travelled to Taiwan to participate in the festival and a public conversation, creating a genuinely two-way curatorial relationship. At the same time, GLOWBALL continued to develop programmes in collaboration with different cultural scenes. Formosa Sound System once again created an independent sonic environment rooted in sound system culture. Taiwanese-Japanese art collective TOTEI brought together party culture and new media art through exhibitions, VJ performances, and late-night programming. Communities including isaNight, Ballroom, and drag performers also continued to take part, bringing local and international artists and audiences together on the same platform. Compared with the stage-based and scene-based collaborations of the previous year, partnerships in 2026 began to expand into co-curation, artist exchange, exhibition production, and knowledge sharing. Internationalization, in this sense, is no longer simply about increasing the number of overseas artists on the line-up. It is a process of gradually building sustained working relationships between different cities, cultural organizations, and creative communities. From Lyon in May and Taipei in June to continued industry and curatorial exchanges at TMEX in August, GLOWBALL has gradually evolved from an annual music festival into a platform connecting Taiwanese creators, Asian cultural scenes, and international cultural networks. Electronic Music as a Meeting Point for Different Cultural Scenes Global club, bass music, gqom, house, techno, experimental electronics, live music, traditional instrumentation, and various forms of cross-genre creation have all appeared throughout different editions of GLOWBALL. Rather than using genre as the festival’s primary organizing principle, GLOWBALL approaches electronic music as a cultural interface — a space through which different creative communities can encounter one another and form new relationships. DJs and dancers, musicians and new media artists, Ballroom and drag communities, Taiwanese creators and international curators each operate within their own professional networks and cultural contexts. A festival can create a shared time and space in which these otherwise separate networks begin to overlap. From Producing Programs to Building Cultural Networks Taiwan has active communities across independent music, new media art, DJ and VJ culture, dance, performance, and a wide range of subcultures. New creators and cultural practices continue to emerge. Yet different disciplines often have their own languages, audiences, and professional networks. Cross-disciplinary collaboration—as well as longer-term exchange with other Asian cities and European cultural scenes—requires time and sustained commitment. Over the past three years, GLOWBALL has therefore gradually placed greater emphasis not only on programming, but also on building relationships: connecting different music and art scenes, maintaining exchanges with international festivals and curatorial organizations, facilitating interdisciplinary co-production, and creating opportunities for creators from different cultural networks to meet and collaborate. These efforts are not intended to represent Taiwan’s electronic music culture as a whole, and GLOWBALL itself remains in an ongoing process of exploration and learning. Rather, the festival hopes to serve as one small but sustainable node within a much larger cultural network — continuously creating possibilities for exchange between artists, communities, and international networks within the scope of what it can realistically contribute. Looking Ahead GLOWBALL is currently preparing and exploring the next stage of its development. Moving forward, it will continue to take electronic music as a point of departure while expanding collaborations with different artistic disciplines, cultural communities, and international partners. These directions are still taking shape, and GLOWBALL looks forward to continuing to develop new possibilities for exchange and collaboration with like-minded artists, curators, media, and partner organizations. items.body: Metanoia, Yulianna Avdeeva’s new album for Pentatone, focuses on the transformation of Liszt’s style between his Weimar and late periods. Liszt had already shown an experimental curiosity with structure and form in the Sonata in B minor—a work presented here alongside later pieces such as the Bagatelle sans tonalité and Nuages gris. Metanoia Amazon Presto Apple Given the many versions available, Avdeeva’s B minor sonata is impressive. Some renditions are either entirely too heavy or too light, but hers strikes a sensible balance of power, speed, and musicality. There are admittedly some moments where velocity comes at the expense of clarity, but the furious and urgent spirit is aptly captured. Avdeeva shows firm command in the first section (track 1). The octave passages are bold and brash, while the runs remain light, agile, and effortless. I did find the lead-up to the second theme somewhat rushed: the Grandioso (track 2) is rousing but needs more breadth for us to fully appreciate the arrival of the D major section—something Argerich’s 1971 recording does so well. The more tender moments of the section, however, are exquisitely rendered with translucent passagework. Fortunately, Avdeeva does not rush the Andante (track 3). Its blend of nostalgia, reverie, and introspection offers a much-needed respite from the frenetic parts of the sonata and leaves enough space for the return of drama in the finale. The fugue (track 4), meticulous in its rhythm and articulation, gives a powerful drive back to the recapitulation but never leaves us with any sense of uncomfortable volatility. The late works begin with La lugubre gondola II (track 5), whose origins are as dark as the music. In 1882, Liszt is said to have had an eerie vision that his son-in-law Richard Wagner would die and that his body would be carried on a black gondola. The vision came true a few months later, in early 1883. Avdeeva reflects the grim nature of this realization as she highlights the starkness of the sparse textures and the austerity, foreboding, and finality of the monophony. The work is as much an homage to Wagner as it is a premonition, and the second half is where we hear more elements of tonality and lyricism. R.W. – Venezia (track 9), the companion work to La lugubre gondola, was written after Wagner’s death. While just as somber and still minimalistic, the piece lies largely in the lower register. Avdeeva gives the left-hand octave ostinato plenty of depth but also a necessary sense of severity. The brighter Bagatelle sans tonalité (track 6) recalls the showmanship of earlier works, though the bravado now takes the form of a more elegant virtuosity. The unmistakable element of caprice is well evoked. Yulianna Avdeeva. Photo © Kevin Kinzley. Nuages gris (track 7), like La lugubre gondola, has sinister undertones amid its minimalism. Avdeeva still finds a way to create some breathtaking tone colors; the final two mysterious chords are a good example, offering a fleeting sense of whimsy quite different from the ominous mood that pervades most of the piece. The Hungarian Rhapsody No. 17 (track 10), written just a few years before Liszt’s death, diverges considerably in character from the earlier rhapsodies, Nos. 1–15. The flamboyant, fiery, and playful profile gives way to more ominous undertones and an atonal base. Avdeeva brings out a threatening and even aggressive nature: accents and dissonances carry a stinging sharpness, and the octave passages at the end are adamant and tumultuous. Unstern! – Sinistre (track 11) is perhaps the most jarring of the late pieces, owing to its harsh atonality and even harsher textures. The accents and chords here are abrasive (as they should be), yet never become too strident on the ears. Unlike some of the other works, whose endings offer some form of catharsis, the latter sections here only prolong the doubt and disquiet, a distinction Avdeeva makes clear. The juxtaposition of works from different eras is well judged. In one sitting, the heavy mood of the late works may become a bit overbearing, but this only goes to show the effectiveness of Avdeeva’s interpretations. All in all, a series of excellent performances that should find a place on the shelf of any Liszt enthusiast. items.body: Norwegian gothic industrial metal act Gothminister release the album “We Are All Demons” on 16 October 2026 via Elevator Records, distributed through The Orchard. The 11-track record is the project’s ninth studio album. Frontman Bjørn Alexander Brem recorded, produced, mixed and mastered “We Are All Demons” entirely himself, the first time he has handled the full process alone. Musically, the album combines gothic industrial metal with EDM elements, synthesizers, industrial guitars, theatrical vocals, female duets and choral passages. Lyrically, it addresses inner darkness and the parts of the self normally kept beneath the surface. Tracklist: Darkest Side of Earth We Are All Demons Nightmare King The Dark The Spell Welcome to Hell Salsa My Revenge Darkness Is My Throne Fearless There’s a Crown for All “We Are All Demons” follows the single “My Revenge,” released from the album on 31 July 2026. The album is available for pre-order via The Orchard’s smart link. A digipak CD edition is also listed through Napalm Records’ webshop. Gothminister has confirmed the following live dates around the release: Tour dates for Gothminister’s ‘We Are All Demons’ release 16 October 2026: Fiskepiren, Stavanger, Norway 19 November 2026: Parkteatret, Oslo, Norway 20-21 November 2026: Hellsinki Industrial Festival, Helsinki, Finland More dates are expected to be announced. About Gothminister Gothminister was formed in Oslo, Norway, in 1999 by Bjørn Alexander Brem, who handles lead vocals, programming and instruments. Guitarist Glenn Nilsen is the project’s other current member. The band’s studio discography includes “Gothic Electronic Anthems” (2003), “Empire of Dark Salvation” (2005), “Happiness in Darkness” (2008), “Anima Inferna” (2011), “Utopia” (2013), “The Other Side” (2017), “Pandemonium” (2022) and “Pandemonium II: The Battle of the Underworlds” (2024). Gothminister was also a candidate in Norway’s 2024 Eurovision Song Contest selection, Melodi Grand Prix. “We Are All Demons” follows “Pandemonium II: The Battle of the Underworlds” from 2024 and arrives 16 October 2026 via Elevator Records.

items.body: Cork, Ireland duo Crá Croí release the single “Just Another Day” on 2 October 2026, on Bandcamp and streaming platforms. It is the third and last single from the duo’s debut album, “Tá Brón Orm,” due 30 October 2026. “Just Another Day” addresses what the duo describe as a cynical view of modern life, where emotions feel performative and authenticity is replaced by “superficial substitutes.” Crá Croí is entirely self-produced by the duo, credited as RG and CD, who also direct their own videos and artwork. Side-Line previously covered the duo’s single “Lord Of The Wild” in July 2026. About Crá Croí Crá Croí is a Cork, Ireland duo whose name translates from Irish as “torment of the heart.” The project is self-produced from music to visuals by its two members, credited as RG and CD. Side-Line covered the duo’s single “Lord Of The Wild” in July 2026. “Just Another Day,” released 2 October 2026, is the third and final single from the duo’s debut album, “Tá Brón Orm,” due 30 October 2026.
items._cn_summary: 爱尔兰科克二人组 Crá Croí（爱尔兰语意为"心的折磨"）以全自制的模式发布了首张专辑《Tá Brón Orm》的第三支单曲《Just Another Day》。这首歌据描述表达了对现代生活的犬儒看法，指出情感在当代变得表演化，真实性被表层替代品所取代。整张专辑从音乐到视觉均由两位成员 RG 与 CD 自行创作完成，体现出独立 DIY 的美学取向。从可获取信息来看，这是一篇典型的新闻通告而非乐评，缺乏对声音设计、编曲手法、乐器编排等具体音乐层面的描述，无法判断其是否真正触及实验、暗潮或电子融合的核心。Side-Line 作为来源偏向暗潮/工业领域，但文章本身仅提供了发行信息和主题概述，深度极为有限。

items.body: Psalm 68 says Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to Elohim, one of the Hebrew Bible’s names for God, and Rastafari read the verse as prophecy, fulfilled when Haile Selassie I took the Ethiopian throne in 1930. Julian Asher, a reggae singer from Cape Town now living in Berlin, paraphrased it in the notes to his debut EP, Haile Abeba Sound, and on “Elohim” he builds a whole song around the name. He sings of a He and a She arriving at full strength to reclaim an ancient throne from those who lead people astray, and calls on Abba and Selassie I by name across the verses. The music comes from Downtown Steppas, a Berlin backing band who also build their own riddims. The partnership goes back to “Perilous” in 2022, and “Just Cause”, a single Asher cut over the band’s Fantasia riddim, now shares its name with their first album together. Just Cause was recorded last winter, from songs singer and band had been playing together for years. Stream “Elohim” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Julian Asher & Downtown Steppas – Elohim appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 南非开普敦雷鬼歌手Julian Asher现居柏林，与柏林伴奏乐队Downtown Steppas合作推出专辑《Just Cause》，单曲《Elohim》以希伯来圣经中上帝之名展开创作主题，歌词引用诗篇第68节关于埃塞俄比亚的预言，涉及拉斯塔法里教义中海尔·塞拉西一世登基的历史叙事。歌曲由乐队自行构建riddim伴奏，两人合作可追溯至2022年的单曲《Perilous》，专辑录制于去年冬季，收录了歌手与乐队多年积累的共同曲目。整体风格属于传统根派雷鬼与dub范畴，带有南非与埃塞俄比亚文化交叉的叙事视角，但在声音设计与实验层面未见显著突破。

items.body: Review by JuanSaavedra — I was lucky enough to receive a promo copy of this album ahead of its October 2nd release through ARQUEN Records (many thanks, the guys from Spain are always so generous and I am very grateful), and I had already fallen for the three singles before hearing the full thing. So by the time I sat down with Datura Lodge in its entirety, I came in with high expectations. And somehow they were exceeded.2026 has been, honestly, a somewhat quiet year for new progressive rock releases that have genuinely grabbed me, while I wait for the new Steven Wilson album, which I am very much looking forward to. Which makes it all the more satisfying when something like this arrives. And curiously, reading the credits of this album, I discover that drummer Russell Holzman is also the drummer on the upcoming Steven Wilson record, and that his father Adam Holzman, whose career includes Miles Davis and Steven Wilson himself, plays keyboards here. A detail that says a lot about the calibre of this project.Nicky B and "W", the New Jersey duo at the heart of this project, have put together a debut that feels both deeply rooted in the tradition and completely alive in the present. The reference points are there if you want to find them. There is something of Genesis in the quieter, more introspective passages, and when the vocalist climbs to his upper register, the resemblance to Phil Collins is striking in the best possible way. There are moments that bring Porcupine Tree and Steven Wilson to mind, particularly in the layered textures and the way the album handles emotional weight. And Pink Floyd surfaces here and there, mostly in the atmosphere rather than anything overt. But none of this sounds like pastiche. It sounds like a band that has absorbed all of this and made something genuinely their own.The album opens with a trio of tracks, "Mummy", "Stone" and "98 and 94", that flow into each other almost like a suite and hook you before you even realise it. The middle section gets more direct and rock-driven, with "Can" and "Them" showing another side of the duo, harder-hitting and with that energy that recalls Rush. And "Hole", the third single, has that unmistakable Floydian atmosphere, a slow emotional build that keeps growing until the guitar solo says everything the words could not.But it is "Lodge", the closing track, that for me ties everything together. It starts with an acoustic delicacy that evokes the best moments of Genesis, and from there it grows into something wider and more modern without ever losing the melodic thread. It is the most complete track on the album and a finale that stays with you for days. Ben Karas also leaves an electrifying violin on "Stone" that is one of the most memorable moments of the whole listen.The album flows perfectly, has an ideal running time and not a single moment of filler. One of the most addictive listens I have had all year, and one I keep returning to without any sense of it diminishing. I can't wait to see where this band goes next. What a debut. Awesome album.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自新泽西二人组的处女作，定位为重型前卫摇滚。乐评将其与Genesis、Phil Collins、Porcupine Tree、Steven Wilson、Pink Floyd、Rush等经典前卫摇滚血脉相联系，指出乐队在继承传统的同时融入了当代质感。鼓手Russell Holzman同时参与了即将发行的Steven Wilson新专辑，键盘手Adam Holzman曾与Miles Davis合作，这一家族背景为专辑增添了专业分量。曲目编排注重流畅过渡，开篇三首形成套曲结构，中段转向更直接的摇滚能量，末曲以原声开篇逐渐扩展。小提琴在《Stone》中的表现被特别提及。整体而言，这是一张在传统前卫摇滚框架内完成度较高的作品，旋律性强、结构完整，但与用户偏好的实验、电子、暗潮、爵士即兴等方向存在明显距离，更偏向学院化的复古致敬路线。
